newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Malaysia bids for trade with southern Africa.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia bids for trade with southern Africa.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir bin Mohamad, vigorously pursuing trade and commercial links with southern Africa, jetted into Botswana at the weekend to pass on his country's development concept.

Mahathir was in Kasane, Botswana, on Sunday as a special guest at the three-day First Southern Africa International Dialogue on Smart Partnership for the Generation of Wealth, which opens in the evening.
Conceived in Malaysia, "Smart Partnerships" is the philosophy of creating "win-win" relationships and promoting "cooperative competitiveness."
It is based on the premise that governments, private sector organisations and individuals must work together for long-term mutual gains.
"Malaysia sees new friends in Africa," he told leaders of the 12-member Southern African Development Community's business community in the Botswana capital, Gaborone, on Saturday night.

Singling out his host country, Mahathir said: "Malaysia's approach to economic growth can work in Botswana, with some modifications... We in Malaysia are encouraged by the economic and fiscal reforms undertaken by the government of Botswana."
Current trade between Botswana and Malaysia is modest. It has increased from $17,500 in 1992 to $541,000 in 1996, mostly in imports to Botswana of Malaysian veterinary drugs, soap and plastic goods.
Mahathir suggested that Malaysians should now consider investing in the exploitation of the untapped mining resources of Botswana whose mining industry accounts for 80 percent of all export revenues.
The Botswana government in turn should boost efforts to support the private sector, he said.
President Sir Ketumile Masire of Botswana will officially open the conference, due to be attended by 14 African nations and over 200 business leaders, at 2030 local time/1830 GMT on Sunday.

The 12 SADC member states of Angola, Botswana, Lesotho, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Swaziland, Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe as well as Uganda and Ghana will be represented at the conference.
